item.mechanism: Precipitation strengthening via coherent L12 gamma-prime precipitates with high volume fraction and high anti-phase boundary (APB) energy.
item.system: HESA (Ni47.9Al10.2Co16.9Cr7.4Fe8.9Ti5.8Mo0.9Nb1.2W0.4C0.4 at%) with 69 vol% gamma' precipitates.
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature to 800 °C tensile testing; solution and aging heat-treated state.
item.supporting_observation: The authors calculate APB energy of HESA (0.22 J/m2) is higher than CMSX-2 (0.19 J/m2) and note that higher APB energy contributes to strengthening, though the gamma' size (290 nm) is below the optimized size for peak strength.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism is less effective at peak strength compared to CMSX-2 because the gamma' size (290 nm) is smaller than the estimated optimized size (390 nm) for HESA; strength could increase by 16% if size increased.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors consider that the lower degree of lattice misfit in HESA (0.08%) compared to CMSX-2 (-0.33%) also contributes to the slightly lower yield strength of HESA.
quotes: The tensile strength of HESA can be attributed to the high volume fraction of strengthening precipitates γ′
higher APB energy of γ′ may contribute to some degree of strengthening in HESA
the optimized size of γ′ in HESA should be around 390 nm; however, the as heat-treated γ′ size is only 290 nm

item.mechanism: Strengthening due to low stacking fault energy (SFE) of the FCC matrix, which increases partial dislocation spacing and makes dislocation bowing around precipitates more difficult.
item.system: HESA matrix with estimated SFE of 0.7 J/m2.
item.operating_conditions: High temperature creep at 750, 850, and 982 °C under 159 MPa.
item.supporting_observation: The authors estimate SFE reduction due to alloying is 1.5 times greater in HESA than CMSX-2, leading to an estimated SFE of 0.7 J/m2, which correlates with lower creep rates.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism is proposed for intermediate temperatures where no rafting occurs; at 982 °C, rafting dominates the creep behavior.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors consider that sluggish diffusion in the high entropy matrix also contributes to higher activation energy and lower creep rates.
quotes: lower SFE of γ matrix in HESA can be expected, as the generally reported low SFEs of HEAs
For materials possessing lower SFE, partial dislocations are more energetically favorable, and the spacing between partial dislocations can be increased
the dislocations bowing around γ′ particles would become more difficult, which effectively decreases the creep strain rate

item.mechanism: Creep deformation dominated by thermally activated bypassing of dislocations around gamma' precipitates via climb and glide in the gamma matrix, rather than shearing.
item.operating_conditions: Creep at 750 °C and 850 °C under 159 MPa for up to 800 h.
item.supporting_observation: No obvious primary creep regime was observed, and TEM analysis showed dislocations piled up in the matrix without shearing the precipitates.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism does not apply at 982 °C where parallel rafting occurs and tertiary creep dominates.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors explicitly rule out the dislocation shearing gamma' mechanism due to the lack of primary creep.
quotes: no obvious primary creep is observed, demonstrating that the dislocation shearing γ′ mechanism should not be applicable
thermally activated by-passing of dislocations around γ′ precipitates should be the deformation mechanism
the inelastic deformation can essentially concentrate within the γ regions, where dislocations move by climb and glide processes to pass by γ′ particles

item.mechanism: Accelerated creep and tertiary creep dominance caused by positive lattice misfit leading to parallel (P-) rafting of gamma' precipitates along the stress axis.
item.system: HESA with positive lattice misfit (δ = 0.08%) at 982 °C.
item.supporting_observation: TEM and SEM images showed gamma' coarsening into plate-like morphology parallel to the stress axis (from 0.29 μm to 3 μm length), and creep curves showed extensive tertiary creep without primary creep.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism is specific to high temperatures where positive misfit drives rafting; it competes with the strengthening effect of un-rafted precipitates at lower temperatures.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors contrast this with CMSX-2 which exhibits negative misfit and perpendicular (N-) rafting, which provides better creep resistance via interfacial dislocation networks.
quotes: Positive misfit between FCC matrix and precipitate has yielded parallel raft microstructure during creep at 982 °C
the creep curves of HESA were dominated by tertiary creep behavior
higher creep rate of HESA compared to that of CMSX-2 could be a result of P-raft

item.mechanism: Enhanced creep resistance at intermediate temperatures due to sluggish diffusion in the high entropy matrix leading to higher activation energy for creep.
item.system: HESA with high mixing entropy (ΔS_mix = 1.60 R).
item.supporting_observation: The calculated activation energy for creep in HESA (290 kJ/mol) is higher than that of CMSX-2 (230 kJ/mol), which the authors attribute to sluggish diffusion.
item.scope_limits: The benefit of sluggish diffusion is offset at 982 °C by the detrimental effect of parallel rafting.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors consider that the stable gamma' morphology at lower temperatures also contributes to resistance, independent of diffusion.
quotes: the possible sluggish diffusion of the higher entropy γ matrix and the un-rafted γ′ microstructure can contribute to lower creep rate
the sluggish diffusion of the high entropy γ matrix may have attributed to the higher creep activation energy

item.mechanism: Microstructural stability against topologically-close-packed (TCP) phase formation and high gamma' solvus temperature maintaining strength.
item.system: HESA with high entropy matrix and L12 precipitates.
item.operating_conditions: Thermal exposure from 700 to 1100 °C for at least 500 h; gamma' solvus at 1199 °C.
item.supporting_observation: DTA curves show gamma' solvus at 1199 °C, and previous studies cited indicate stability against TCP phases from 700 to 1100 °C.
item.scope_limits: The text notes that while stable, the gamma' size in the current study (290 nm) is not optimized for peak strength.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors mention that other HEAs suffer from phase instability associated with L21, B2, and Cu-rich FCC phases.
quotes: the γ - γ′ microstructure of HESAs can remain stable against topologically-close-packed (TCP) phase formation from 700 to 1100 °C for at least 500 h
with enhanced γ′ solvus temperatures above 1150 °C
the γ′ solvus and solidus temperature are 1199 and 1276 °C, respectively

item.mechanism: Ductile fracture via dimple formation in the matrix, with minor brittle fracture associated with carbides.
item.operating_conditions: Creep at 982 °C under 159 MPa until rupture (114 h).
item.supporting_observation: SEM fractographs showed a rough surface with majority dimple features, but minor facet-like brittle regions near carbides.
item.scope_limits: The brittle fracture is localized to carbide regions; the bulk behavior is ductile.
item.alternatives_considered: None explicitly stated as alternatives, but the presence of carbides is noted as the source of brittle regions.
quotes: the fracture surface is rough and with the majority dimple feature corresponding to ductile behaviour
minor brittle fracture regions reflected by facet-like morphology can be observed associated with the presence of carbides
The diameter of the fractured gauge region has decreased from the original 6.35 mm to 4.75 mm, which demonstrates a ductile necking behavior before fracture

item.mechanism: Strengthening via solid-solution strengthening from minor additions of Mo and W.
item.system: HESA with minor Mo (0.9 at%) and W (0.4 at%).
item.operating_conditions: As-cast and heat-treated state (general mechanical properties).
item.supporting_observation: The authors state in the Methods section that minor amounts of Mo and W are added specifically for solid-solution strengthening.
item.scope_limits: The text does not quantify the specific contribution of Mo/W to the yield strength compared to precipitation or SFE effects.
item.alternatives_considered: The authors note that refractory elements can promote TCP phases, so their fraction was kept low (<1 vol% TCP) to avoid detrimental effects.
quotes: minor amounts of Mo and W are added for solid-solution strengthening
since the addition of refractory elements can easily promote the formation of detrimental topological-close packed (TCP) phases
the fraction of TCP was designed to be less than 1 vol% while adjusting the refractory additions
